metadata.title: Johnson-Lindenstrauss Lemma, Linear and Nonlinear Random Projections, Random Fourier Features, and Random Kitchen Sinks: Tutorial and Survey
metadata.authors: Benyamin Ghojogh, Ali Ghodsi, Fakhri Karray, Mark Crowley

nodes.name: Linear Projection
nodes.statement: For $\b{x} \in \mathbb{R}^d$ and $\b{U} \in \mathbb{R}^{d \times p}$, the projection (hat) matrix is $\b{\Pi} := \b{U}(\b{U}^\top \b{U})^{-1}\b{U}^\top$, giving reconstruction $\widehat{\b{x}} = \b{\Pi}\b{x}$.
nodes.statement_clean: Defines the orthogonal projection matrix onto the column space of U.

nodes.name: Linear Random Projection
nodes.statement: A function $f: \mathbb{R}^d \to \mathbb{R}^p$, $f: \b{x} \mapsto \b{U}^\top \b{x}$, where the entries $u_{jt}$ of $\b{U}$ are i.i.d. with zero mean and (possibly scaled) unit variance; e.g. $u_{jt} \sim \mathcal{N}(0,1)$.
nodes.statement_clean: Random linear map whose projection matrix has i.i.d. zero-mean entries.

nodes.name: Johnson-Lindenstrauss Lemma
nodes.statement: For any $\mathcal{X} = \{\b{x}_i\}_{i=1}^n \subset \mathbb{R}^d$ and $0<\epsilon<1$, if $p \geq \Omega(\ln(n)/(\epsilon^2-\epsilon^3))$, there exists a linear map $f: \mathbb{R}^d \to \mathbb{R}^p$ such that $(1-\epsilon)\|\b{x}_i-\b{x}_j\|_2^2 \leq \|f(\b{x}_i)-f(\b{x}_j)\|_2^2 \leq (1+\epsilon)\|\b{x}_i-\b{x}_j\|_2^2$ with probability $\geq 1-\delta$, where $\delta=2e^{-(\epsilon^2-\epsilon^3)(p/4)}$.
nodes.statement_clean: Random linear projection into O(log n / eps^2) dimensions preserves all pairwise distances up to (1 +/- eps).
assumptions: Entries of $\b{U}$ are i.i.d. with mean zero and (scaled) unit variance, e.g. $u_{ij} \sim \mathcal{N}(0, 1/p)$
conclusions: There exists a linear map $f$ with $(1-\epsilon)\|\b{x}_i-\b{x}_j\|_2^2 \leq \|f(\b{x}_i)-f(\b{x}_j)\|_2^2 \leq (1+\epsilon)\|\b{x}_i-\b{x}_j\|_2^2$ for all pairs

nodes.name: Proof of JL Lemma
nodes.statement: Three-step proof: (1) random projection preserves distances in expectation; (2) bound the deviation probability for one pair via Markov + chi-squared MGF; (3) apply Bonferroni union bound over the $\binom{n}{2}$ pairs.

nodes.name: Distance preserved in expectation
nodes.statement: Compute $\mathbb{E}[\|f(\b{x}_i)-f(\b{x}_j)\|_2^2]$ using $\mathbb{E}[u_{kt}u_{lt}] = \delta_{kl}/p$ to get $\mathbb{E}[\|f(\b{x}_i)-f(\b{x}_j)\|_2^2] = \|\b{x}_i-\b{x}_j\|_2^2$.

nodes.name: Bound deviation for one pair via chi-squared MGF
nodes.statement: Show $\|\b{U}^\top \b{x}_D\|_2^2/\|\b{x}_D\|_2^2 \sim \chi_p^2/p$. Apply Markov inequality to $e^{\lambda \chi_p^2}$ with optimal $\lambda = \epsilon/(2(1+\epsilon))$ to obtain $\mathbb{P}(\chi_p^2 > (1+\epsilon)p) \leq e^{-(p/4)(\epsilon^2-\epsilon^3)}$.

nodes.name: Union bound over all pairs
nodes.statement: By Bonferroni's inequality over the $\binom{n}{2}=n(n-1)/2$ pairs, $\mathbb{P}(\text{error}) \leq n(n-1) e^{-(p/4)(\epsilon^2-\epsilon^3)} \leq \delta'$.

nodes.name: Lower bound on subspace dimensionality
nodes.statement: The dimensionality $p$ must satisfy $p \geq \Omega(\ln(n)/(\epsilon^2-\epsilon^3))$ for the JL bound on probability of error to hold.

nodes.name: Proof of dimensionality lower bound
nodes.statement: Setting $\mathbb{P}(\text{error}) = n(n-1) e^{-(p/4)(\epsilon^2-\epsilon^3)} \leq \delta'$ and solving for $p$ yields $p \geq (8\ln n - 4\ln\delta')/(\epsilon^2-\epsilon^3)$.

nodes.name: Concentration of Measure
nodes.statement: $\mathbb{P}((1-\epsilon)\|\b{x}\|_2^2 \leq \|\b{U}^\top \b{x}\|_2^2 \leq (1+\epsilon)\|\b{x}\|_2^2) \geq 1 - 2e^{-c\epsilon^2 p}$ for a Gaussian random matrix $\b{U} \in \mathbb{R}^{d \times p}$ with constant $c>0$.
nodes.statement_clean: Norm-preservation inequality for Gaussian random matrices, equivalent to JL.

nodes.name: Probability bound on projected norm via beta
nodes.statement: Let $p<d$, $L=\|\b{z}_D\|_2^2$ for $\b{z}_D$ the random projection of $\b{x}_D$ onto a $p$-dim subspace. If $\beta<1$, $\mathbb{P}(L \leq \beta p/d) \leq \exp((p/2)(1-\beta+\ln\beta))$; if $\beta>1$, $\mathbb{P}(L \geq \beta p/d) \leq \exp((p/2)(1-\beta+\ln\beta))$.
assumptions: $L = \|\b{z}_D\|_2^2$ where $\b{z}_D$ is the random projection of $\b{x}_D = \b{x}_i-\b{x}_j$

nodes.name: Order of probability of success for random projection
nodes.statement: If $p \geq 4(\epsilon^2/2 - \epsilon^3/3)^{-1}\ln(n) = \Omega(\ln(n)/(\epsilon^2-\epsilon^3))$, then with probability of order $\mathcal{O}(1/n^2)$, local distances are not distorted by random projection more than $(1\pm\epsilon)$.
conclusions: The probability of error in random projection is $\mathcal{O}(1/n^2)$

nodes.name: Proof of order of probability of success
nodes.statement: Two-sided bound: apply Lemma LP454.2 with $\beta=1-\epsilon$ (lower side) and $\beta=1+\epsilon$ (upper side), use logarithm bounds $\ln(1-x) \leq -(x+x^2/2)$ and $\ln(1+x) \leq x - x^2/2 + x^3/3$, conclude each side is $\leq 1/n^2$.

nodes.name: Lower-side bound (beta < 1)
nodes.statement: Set $\beta=1-\epsilon$. By Lemma LP454.2, $\mathbb{P}(\cdots \leq (1-\epsilon)(p/d)\|\cdots\|^2) \leq \exp((p/2)(\epsilon+\ln(1-\epsilon))) \leq \exp(-p\epsilon^2/4) \leq \exp(-2\ln n) = 1/n^2$.

nodes.name: Upper-side bound (beta > 1)
nodes.statement: Set $\beta=1+\epsilon$. By Lemma LP454.2, $\mathbb{P}(\cdots \geq (1+\epsilon)(p/d)\|\cdots\|^2) \leq \exp(-(p/2)(\epsilon^2/2-\epsilon^3/3)) \leq \exp(-2\ln n) = 1/n^2$.

nodes.name: With High Probability (w.h.p.)
nodes.statement: When the probability of success in an algorithm goes to one as the input information or a parameter is increased to infinity, the algorithm is correct with high probability (w.h.p.).

nodes.name: Distance preservation for k-sparse signals
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal{S}_k = \{\b{x} \in \mathbb{R}^d: \#\{i:|x_i|>0\} \leq k\}$. If $p = \mathcal{O}(\epsilon^{-2} k\ln(d/k))$, then $f(\b{x}) = \b{U}^\top \b{x}$ satisfies $(1-\epsilon)\|\b{x}_i-\b{x}_j\|_2^2 \leq \|f(\b{x}_i)-f(\b{x}_j)\|_2^2 \leq (1+\epsilon)\|\b{x}_i-\b{x}_j\|_2^2$ for all $\b{x}_i,\b{x}_j \in \mathcal{S}_k$ w.h.p.; error probability $2(12/\epsilon)^k e^{-(p/2)(\epsilon^2/8-\epsilon^3/24)}$.

nodes.name: Restricted Isometry Property (RIP)
nodes.statement: $f: \mathbb{R}^d \to \mathbb{R}^p$, $f(\b{x})=\b{U}^\top \b{x}$, has RIP of order $k$ and level $\epsilon \in (0,1)$ if $(1-\epsilon)\|\b{x}\|_2^2 \leq \|\b{U}^\top \b{x}\|_2^2 \leq (1+\epsilon)\|\b{x}\|_2^2$ for all $k$-sparse $\b{x} \in \mathbb{R}^d$.

nodes.name: Gaussian random matrix has RIP
nodes.statement: A Gaussian random matrix $\b{U} \in \mathbb{R}^{d \times p}$ has RIP if $p \geq \epsilon^{-2} k\ln(d/k)$.
conclusions: $\b{U}$ has RIP of order $k$ and level $\epsilon$

nodes.name: Sparse JL via diagonal sign flips
nodes.statement: If $f(\b{x}) = \b{U}^\top \b{x}$ satisfies the RIP-type bound for all $k$-sparse $\b{x}$ and $\b{D}_\xi$ is diagonal with $\pm 1$ entries, then $\mathbb{P}((1-\epsilon)\|\b{x}\|_2^2 \leq \|\b{U}^\top \b{D}_\xi \b{x}\|_2^2 \leq (1+\epsilon)\|\b{x}\|_2^2) \geq 1 - 2e^{-c\epsilon^2 p/\ln(d)}$.

nodes.name: RIP + sign flips imply JL up to log(d)
nodes.statement: Comparing Theorem TP454.2 with Definition DP454.3 shows that a random matrix with RIP and random column sign flips implies the JL lemma up to an $\ln(d)$ factor.
assumptions: Random column sign flips applied via $\b{D}_\xi$
conclusions: JL-type concentration holds, with the dimensionality bound differing by an $\ln(d)$ factor

nodes.name: Distance of points w.r.t. norms
nodes.statement: For $n$ i.i.d. random points in $\mathbb{R}^d$, $\lim_{d \to \infty} \mathbb{E}[\text{dist}_{\max,r} - \text{dist}_{\min,r}] = d^{1/r - 1/2}$ where $\text{dist}_{\max,r}$ and $\text{dist}_{\min,r}$ are the max/min distances from the origin under norm $\ell_r$.

nodes.name: $\ell_1$ more meaningful than $\ell_2$ in high dimensions
nodes.statement: For high-dimensional data, the $\ell_1$ norm (Manhattan distance) is more meaningful for nearest-neighbor comparisons than the $\ell_2$ norm (Euclidean distance), since $\ell_1$'s relative max-min difference grows like $d^{1/2}$ while $\ell_2$'s tends to a constant.
conclusions: Under $\ell_1$: max-min distance gap grows like $d^{1/2}$

nodes.name: Proof of $\ell_1$ vs $\ell_2$ corollary
nodes.statement: Apply Lemma LP454.6: for $r=2$ the limit is 1; for $r>2$ the exponent is negative, so the gap vanishes; for $r=1$ the gap grows as $d^{1/2}$.

nodes.name: Extension of JL lemma to any $\ell_r$ norm
nodes.statement: For embedding into $\ell_r$ with $1 \leq r \leq \infty$, there exists a linear $f: \mathbb{R}^d \to \mathbb{R}^p$ with $p \leq d$ satisfying $(p/d)^{|1/r-1/2|}\|\b{x}_i-\b{x}_j\|_r \leq \|\b{U}^\top(\b{x}_i-\b{x}_j)\|_r \leq (d/p)^{|1/r-1/2|}\|\b{x}_i-\b{x}_j\|_r$.
conclusions: There exists linear $f: \mathbb{R}^d \to \mathbb{R}^p$, $f(\b{x})=\b{U}^\top \b{x}$, satisfying the sandwich bound on $\|\cdot\|_r$

nodes.name: Difficulty / impossibility of $\ell_r$ embedding for $r \neq 2$
nodes.statement: The suitable norm for linear random projection is $\ell_2$. Dimensionality reduction with a linear map in $\ell_r$ with $r \neq 2$ is difficult or impossible (only $\ell_2$ gives constant distortion).
conclusions: Distortion is not constant; in $\ell_1$ for example one gets $(p/d)^{1/2}$ distortion
nodes.origin_citation: Lee and Naor 2004; Charikar 2002; Brinkman and Charikar 2005

nodes.name: Proof of $\ell_r$ impossibility corollary
nodes.statement: By Theorem TP454.3, $\|\b{U}^\top(\b{x}_i-\b{x}_j)\|_2 \approx \|\b{x}_i-\b{x}_j\|_2$ (constant distortion), but for $r=1$ the bound becomes $(p/d)^{1/2}\|\b{x}_i-\b{x}_j\|_1$ which is not constant distortion.

nodes.name: Restricted Isometry Property-1 (RIP-1)
nodes.statement: For $p \geq c\epsilon^{-2} k\ln(d)$, there exists a linear $f: \mathbb{R}^d \to \mathbb{R}^p$ with $p \leq d$ such that $(1-2\epsilon)\|\b{x}\|_1 \leq \|\b{U}^\top \b{x}\|_1 \leq \|\b{x}\|_1$ for all $k$-sparse $\b{x}$. A matrix $\b{U}$ with this property has RIP-1.

nodes.name: Interpolation Norm $\ell_{1,2,s}$
nodes.statement: Sort entries of $\b{x} \in \mathbb{R}^d$ from largest to smallest, partition the support into $s$ disjoint subsets $\{\mathcal{S}_i\}_{i=1}^s$. Then $\|\b{x}\|_{1,2,s} := \sqrt{\sum_{i=1}^{\lceil n/s \rceil} \|\b{x}_{\mathcal{S}_i}\|_1^2}$.

nodes.name: JL-type bound under interpolation norm
nodes.statement: There exists $f: \mathbb{R}^d \to \mathbb{R}^p$, $f(\b{x}) = \b{U}^\top \b{x}$, such that with probability $\geq 1 - 2d e^{-\epsilon^2 p/s}$, $(0.63-\epsilon)\|\b{x}\|_{1,2,s} \leq \|\b{U}^\top \b{x}\|_1 \leq (1.63+\epsilon)\|\b{x}\|_{1,2,s}$.

nodes.name: Low-Rank Matrix Approximation via Random Projection
nodes.section: 5.1 Low-Rank Matrix Approximation Using Random Projection
nodes.statement: Two-step procedure: (1) compute $\b{Y} = (1/\sqrt{p})\b{U}^\top \b{X}$ with random Gaussian $\b{U} \in \mathbb{R}^{d \times p}$; (2) compute SVD of $\b{Y}$ and form $\widetilde{\b{X}}_p = \b{X}(\sum_{i=1}^p \b{b}_i \b{b}_i^\top)$.

nodes.name: Project X to smaller matrix Y
nodes.statement: Sample i.i.d. standard normal entries for $\b{U} \in \mathbb{R}^{d \times p}$; compute $\b{Y} = (1/\sqrt{p})\b{U}^\top \b{X} \in \mathbb{R}^{p \times n}$.

nodes.name: Compute SVD of Y and form rank-p approximation
nodes.statement: Compute $\b{Y} = \b{A}\b{\Lambda}\b{B}^\top$. Set $\widetilde{\b{X}}_p = \b{X}(\sum_{i=1}^p \b{b}_i\b{b}_i^\top)$.

nodes.name: Singular values of Y close to those of X
nodes.statement: Let $\b{X} = \b{C}\b{\Sigma}\b{E}^\top$ be the SVD of $\b{X}$ and $\b{X}_p$ its top-$p$ truncation. If $p \geq c\ln(n)/\epsilon^2$, then $\sum_{i=1}^p \lambda_i^2 \geq (1-\epsilon)\sum_{i=1}^p \sigma_i^2 = (1-\epsilon)\|\b{X}_p\|_F^2$.

nodes.name: Low-rank approximation error bound
nodes.statement: $\|\b{X}-\widetilde{\b{X}}_p\|_F^2 \leq \|\b{X}-\b{X}_p\|_F^2 + 2\epsilon\|\b{X}_p\|_F^2$.
assumptions: $\b{X}_p$ is the true rank-$p$ SVD truncation

nodes.name: Proof of low-rank approximation error bound
nodes.statement: Express $\|\b{X}-\widetilde{\b{X}}_p\|_F^2 = \|\b{X}\|_F^2 - \sum_{i=1}^p \|\b{X}\b{b}_i\|_2^2$, combine with $\|\b{X}-\b{X}_p\|_F^2 = \|\b{X}\|_F^2 - \|\b{X}_p\|_F^2$, then apply JL inequality on $\b{U}^\top \b{X}\b{b}_i$ together with Lemma LP454.7 to bound the discrepancy by $2\epsilon\|\b{X}_p\|_F^2$.

nodes.name: Express Frobenius residuals via SVD basis
Apply JL inequality and Lemma LP454.7
nodes.statement: From $\sum_{i=1}^p \|\b{Y}\b{b}_i\|_2^2 = \sum_{i=1}^p \lambda_i^2$ and JL: $\lambda_i^2 \leq (1+\epsilon)\|\b{X}\b{b}_i\|_2^2$. Combined with Lemma LP454.7 yields $\sum_{i=1}^p \|\b{X}\b{b}_i\|_2^2 \geq (1-2\epsilon)\|\b{X}_p\|_F^2$.

nodes.name: Combine to obtain final bound
nodes.statement: Therefore $\|\b{X}_p\|_F^2 - \sum_{i=1}^p \|\b{X}\b{b}_i\|_2^2 \leq 2\epsilon\|\b{X}_p\|_F^2$, hence $\|\b{X}-\widetilde{\b{X}}_p\|_F^2 \leq \|\b{X}-\b{X}_p\|_F^2 + 2\epsilon\|\b{X}_p\|_F^2$.

nodes.name: Time complexity of random-projection low-rank approximation
nodes.statement: The time complexity of low-rank approximation (rank $p$) of $\b{X}$ via random projection is $\mathcal{O}(dn\ln(n))$, much better than $\mathcal{O}(dn^2)$ for plain SVD on $\b{X}$.

nodes.name: Random projection onto hypercube
nodes.statement: For binary $\b{x} \in \mathbb{Z}_2^d$ projected as $f(\b{x}) = \b{U}^\top \b{x} \bmod 2$ with random binary $\b{U} \in \{0,1\}^{d \times p}$ (entries Bernoulli with prob. $\xi = \epsilon^2/\ell$), $p = O(\ln(n)/\epsilon^2)$: piecewise bounds on $\|f(\b{x}_i)-f(\b{x}_j)\|_H$ relative to $\|\b{x}_i-\b{x}_j\|_H$ hold with probability $\geq 1 - e^{-c\epsilon^4 p}$.
assumptions: $\b{U} \in \{0,1\}^{d \times p}$ with i.i.d. Bernoulli entries with parameter $\xi = \epsilon^2/\ell$

nodes.name: $\epsilon$-Approximate Nearest Neighbor Search
nodes.statement: Given dataset $\mathcal{X} = \{\b{x}_i\}_{i=1}^n \subset \mathbb{R}^d$ and query $\b{q}$, return $\b{x}^* \in \mathcal{X}$ satisfying $\|\b{q}-\b{x}^*\|_2 \leq (1+\epsilon)\min_{x\in\mathcal{X}}\|\b{q}-\b{x}\|_2$, or (relaxed form) $\|\b{q}-\b{x}^*\|_2 \leq (1+\epsilon)r$ for user-supplied $r$.

nodes.name: Approximate Nearest Neighbor Search via Random Projection onto Hypercube
nodes.statement: Quantize data to binary; run binary search over distance $r$, performing $k$ independent random projections onto $p$-dim hypercubes for each candidate; compare points via Hamming distance in the projected space.
output: Approximate nearest neighbor $\b{x}^* \in \mathcal{X}$ satisfying $\|\b{q}-\b{x}^*\|_2 \leq (1+\epsilon)r$, or null

nodes.name: Correctness and complexity of approximate NN by random projection
nodes.statement: The hypercube-projection ANN algorithm is correct with probability $1-\delta$. Time complexity $\mathcal{O}((d/\epsilon^4)\ln(n/\delta)\ln(d))$, space $\mathcal{O}(d^2(c_1 n\ln(d))^{c_2/\epsilon^4})$.

nodes.name: Random Fourier Features (RFF)
nodes.section: 6.1 Random Fourier Features for Learning with Approximate Kernels
nodes.statement: Given a positive definite stationary kernel $k$, take its Fourier transform $\widehat{k}$, sample $p$ i.i.d. frequencies $\b{u}_t$ from it, and approximate $k(\b{x},\b{y}) \approx z(\b{x})^\top z(\b{y})$ with $z(\b{x}) = (1/\sqrt{p})[\cos(\b{u}_t^\top \b{x}), \sin(\b{u}_t^\top \b{x})]_t$.
output: Random feature map $z: \mathbb{R}^d \to \mathbb{R}^{2p}$ such that $k(\b{x}, \b{y}) \approx z(\b{x})^\top z(\b{y})$

nodes.name: Compute Fourier transform of kernel
nodes.statement: Compute $\widehat{k}(\b{u}) = (1/(2\pi))\int_{\mathbb{R}^d} e^{-j\b{u}^\top \b{x}} k(\b{x})\, d\b{x}$ and treat $\widehat{k}$ as a probability density.

nodes.name: Sample i.i.d. frequencies
nodes.statement: Draw $p$ i.i.d. frequency vectors $\{\b{u}_t \in \mathbb{R}^d\}_{t=1}^p$ from $\widehat{k}(\b{u})$.

nodes.name: Form random feature map z(x)
nodes.statement: For each $\b{x}$ compute $z(\b{x}) = (1/\sqrt{p})[\cos(\b{u}_1^\top \b{x}), \dots, \cos(\b{u}_p^\top \b{x}), \sin(\b{u}_1^\top \b{x}), \dots, \sin(\b{u}_p^\top \b{x})]^\top \in \mathbb{R}^{2p}$.

nodes.name: Approximate kernel by inner product
nodes.statement: Return $k(\b{x}, \b{y}) \approx z(\b{x})^\top z(\b{y})$ for use in kernel-based learning algorithms.

nodes.name: Uniform error bound for RFF on compact subsets
nodes.statement: For compact $\mathcal{M} \subset \mathbb{R}^d$ with diameter $\text{diam}(\mathcal{M})$, $\mathbb{P}(\sup_{\b{x},\b{y}\in\mathcal{M}}|z(\b{x})^\top z(\b{y}) - k(\b{x},\b{y})| \geq \epsilon) \leq 2^8(\sigma\,\text{diam}(\mathcal{M})/\epsilon)^2 \exp(-p\epsilon^2/(4(d+2)))$, with $\sigma^2 = \mathbb{E}_{\b{u}}[\b{u}^\top \b{u}]$. Required $p \geq \Omega((d/\epsilon^2)\ln(\sigma\,\text{diam}(\mathcal{M})/\epsilon))$.

nodes.name: RFF kernel approximation via Hoeffding
nodes.statement: $\mathbb{P}(|z(\b{x})^\top z(\b{y}) - k(\b{x},\b{y})| \geq \epsilon) \leq 2\exp(-p\epsilon^2/2)$.
nodes.statement_clean: Hoeffding-type pointwise concentration of the RFF kernel approximation.

nodes.name: Random Kitchen Sinks (RKS)
nodes.section: 6.2 Random Kitchen Sinks for Nonlinear Random Projection
nodes.statement: Sample activation parameters $\{w_i\}_{i=1}^p$ i.i.d. from $\mathbb{P}(w)$, then minimize the empirical risk $R_e(\sum_i \alpha_i \phi(\b{x}; w_i))$ over only the output weights $\{\alpha_i\}$ subject to $\|\b{\alpha}\|_\infty \leq c/p$ (or its quadratic regularizer relaxation).
input: Activation function $\phi(\b{x}; w)$ and parameter distribution $\mathbb{P}(w)$

nodes.name: Sample activation parameters
nodes.statement: Sample $\{w_i\}_{i=1}^p$ i.i.d. from distribution $\mathbb{P}(w)$ on parameter space $\Omega$.

nodes.name: Minimize empirical risk over alpha
nodes.statement: Solve $\min_{\b{\alpha}\in\mathbb{R}^p} (1/n)\sum_{i=1}^n \ell(\b{\alpha}^\top \b{g}_i, l_i)$ subject to $\|\b{\alpha}\|_\infty \leq c/p$, or its regularized form $+ \lambda\|\b{\alpha}\|_2^2$.

nodes.name: Form RKS predictor
nodes.statement: Return $\widehat{g}'(\b{x}) = \sum_{i=1}^p \alpha_i\, \phi(\b{x}; w_i)$.

nodes.name: RKS empirical risk objective
nodes.statement: $\min_{\b{\alpha}\in\mathbb{R}^p} (1/n)\sum_{i=1}^n \ell(\b{\alpha}^\top \b{g}_i, l_i) \quad \text{s.t. } \|\b{\alpha}\|_\infty \leq c/p$.

nodes.name: Bound on RKS approximation error
nodes.statement: If $\ell(l,l')$ is $L$-Lipschitz and $g^* \in \mathcal{G}$ minimizes the true risk, then for $\delta>0$, with probability $\geq 1-\delta$ there exists $\widehat{g} \in \widehat{\mathcal{G}}$ such that $R_t(\widehat{g}) - R_t(g^*) \leq (Lc/\sqrt{p})(1 + \sqrt{2\ln(1/\delta)})$.

nodes.name: Bound on RKS estimation error
nodes.statement: If $\ell(l,l') = \ell(l l')$ is $L$-Lipschitz, then for $\delta>0$ and all $\widehat{g} \in \widehat{\mathcal{G}}$, with probability $\geq 1-\delta$, $|R_t(\widehat{g}) - R_e(\widehat{g})| \leq (1/\sqrt{n})(4Lc + 2|\ell(0)| + Lc\sqrt{(1/2)\ln(1/\delta)})$.

nodes.name: Bound on error of RKS
nodes.statement: If activation $\phi$ is bounded ($\sup_{\b{x},w}|\phi(\b{x};w)|\leq 1$) and loss $\ell$ is $L$-Lipschitz, the RKS output $\widehat{g}'$ satisfies $R_t(\widehat{g}') - \min_{g\in\mathcal{G}} R_t(g) \leq \mathcal{O}((1/\sqrt{n} + 1/\sqrt{p})Lc\sqrt{\ln(1/\delta)})$ with probability $\geq 1-2\delta$.

nodes.name: Proof of RKS error bound
nodes.statement: Decompose $R_t(\widehat{g}') - R_t(g^*) \leq |R_t(\widehat{g}') - R_t(\widehat{g}^*)| + (R_t(\widehat{g}^*) - R_t(g^*))$, bound the first term by $2\epsilon_\text{est}$ via Lemma LP454.11 and the second by $\epsilon_\text{app}$ via Lemma LP454.10, then apply Bonferroni's union bound.

nodes.name: Decompose excess risk
nodes.statement: Add and subtract $R_t(\widehat{g}^*)$ to get $R_t(\widehat{g}') - R_t(g^*) \leq |R_t(\widehat{g}')-R_t(\widehat{g}^*)| + R_t(\widehat{g}^*) - R_t(g^*)$.

nodes.name: Bound estimation gap by $2\epsilon_\text{est}$
nodes.statement: By Lemma LP454.11 applied to both $\widehat{g}^*$ and $\widehat{g}'$, plus $R_e(\widehat{g}') \leq R_e(\widehat{g}^*)$, get $|R_t(\widehat{g}') - R_t(\widehat{g}^*)| \leq 2\epsilon_\text{est}$.

nodes.name: Bound approximation gap by $\epsilon_\text{app}$
nodes.statement: By Lemma LP454.10, $R_t(\widehat{g}^*) - R_t(g^*) \leq \epsilon_\text{app} = (Lc/\sqrt{p})(1+\sqrt{2\ln(1/\delta)})$.

nodes.name: Combine via union bound
nodes.statement: Sum the two bounds; by Bonferroni's union bound the failure probability is at most $2\delta$, giving the stated $\mathcal{O}((1/\sqrt{n}+1/\sqrt{p})Lc\sqrt{\ln(1/\delta)})$.

nodes.name: Extreme Learning Machine (ELM)
nodes.statement: Feed-forward neural network whose all layers except the last are randomly weighted; learn only the last-layer weights $\b{\beta}$ via ridge least squares: $\min_{\b{\beta}} \|\b{\beta}^\top \b{H} - \b{T}\|_F^2 + \lambda\|\b{\beta}\|_F^2$.
input: Training data $\{\b{x}_i\}_{i=1}^n$ and one-hot targets $\b{T} \in \mathbb{R}^{p \times n}$
Network architecture and random weights for all but the last layer

nodes.name: ELM ridge regression objective
nodes.statement: $\min_{\b{\beta} \in \mathbb{R}^{d' \times p}} \|\b{\beta}^\top \b{H} - \b{T}\|_F^2 + \lambda\|\b{\beta}\|_F^2$.

nodes.name: Preservation of Euclidean distance by a deterministic layer
nodes.statement: For network layer $\b{U} \in \mathbb{R}^{d \times p}$ with ReLU $g$, $L_1\|\b{x}_i-\b{x}_j\|_2 \leq \|g(\b{U}^\top \b{x}_i) - g(\b{U}^\top \b{x}_j)\|_2 \leq L_2\|\b{x}_i-\b{x}_j\|_2$ where $0 < L_1 \leq L_2$ are Lipschitz constants.

nodes.name: Preservation of Euclidean distance by a random layer
nodes.statement: For random $\b{U} \in \mathbb{R}^{d \times p}$ with i.i.d. Gaussian entries, ReLU $g$, $\mathcal{M} \subset \mathbb{B}_r^d$, and $p \geq c\delta^{-4}w_\mathcal{M}$, with high probability: $|\|g(\b{U}^\top \b{x}_i)-g(\b{U}^\top \b{x}_j)\|_2^2 - ((1/2)\|\b{x}_i-\b{x}_j\|_2^2 + \|\b{x}_i\|_2\|\b{x}_j\|_2 \psi(\b{x}_i,\b{x}_j))| \leq \delta$, with $\psi(\b{x}_i,\b{x}_j) = (1/\pi)(\sin\theta_{i,j} - \theta_{i,j}\cos\theta_{i,j})$.

nodes.name: Preservation of angles by a random layer
nodes.statement: Under the same assumptions as Theorem TP454.9 with $\mathcal{M} \subset \mathbb{B}_1^d \setminus \mathbb{B}_\beta^d$ and $\delta \ll \beta^2 < 1$: $|\cos(\theta'_{i,j}) - (\cos(\theta_{i,j}) + \psi(\b{x}_i,\b{x}_j))| \leq 15\delta/(\beta^2 - 2\delta)$ w.h.p.

nodes.name: Preservation of distances and angles by a random layer
nodes.statement: By a random ReLU layer, for any inputs $\b{x}_i,\b{x}_j$: $(1/2)\|\b{x}_i-\b{x}_j\|_2^2 - \delta \leq \|g(\b{U}^\top \b{x}_i)-g(\b{U}^\top \b{x}_j)\|_2^2 \leq \|\b{x}_i-\b{x}_j\|_2^2 + \delta$ w.h.p.; and an analogous statement holds for angles.
assumptions: Same as Theorems TP454.9 and TP454.10

nodes.name: Proof of distance/angle preservation corollary
nodes.statement: Observe that $\psi(\b{x}_i,\b{x}_j) = 0$ when $\theta_{i,j} = 0$ and $\psi=1$ when $\theta_{i,j}=\pi$. Substituting $\psi=0$ into Theorems TP454.9 and TP454.10 yields the claimed near-isometry of distances and angles when inputs are similar.

nodes.name: Ensemble of Random Projections via Max-Pooling
nodes.statement: Given $m$ random projection matrices $\{\b{U}_j\}_{j=1}^m$, define $f(\b{x}) := \max\{\b{U}_1^\top \b{x}, \dots, \b{U}_m^\top \b{x}\}$ element-wise.

nodes.name: Ensemble of Random Projections for Classification (Schclar-Rokach)
nodes.statement: Sample $m$ random projection matrices $\{\b{U}_j\}$ with normalized columns; for each $\b{U}_j$ project the training data and train a classifier on $(\b{U}_j^\top \b{x}_i, l_i)$; at test time project the query through all $m$ matrices and return the majority vote of the $m$ classifiers' predictions.
output: Ensemble of $m$ trained classifiers; prediction by majority vote

nodes.name: JL is optimal
nodes.statement: It is shown that for any function $f$ satisfying the JL distortion bound, the lower bound $p \geq \Omega(\epsilon^{-2}\ln n)$ holds and need not be random projection; hence the JL lemma is optimal.

nodes.name: Equivalence of JL and concentration of measure
nodes.statement: Comparing the JL probability bound and the concentration-of-measure inequality shows that random projection is equivalent to concentration of measure for Gaussian random matrices.

nodes.name: RKS as a network layer / kernel connection
nodes.statement: RKS models nonlinear random projection as a random network layer; comparing it with the representer theorem reveals a connection between RKS and kernels by identifying $\phi$ as the activation, $\{w_i\}$ as its parameters, and $\{\alpha_i\}$ as the layer weights.
